launcher: Jukebox: a new tab plays the game's music from your disc. Pick a song and a small player appears along the bottom of every page, with previous, play and pause, stop, next, Loop and volume, so the music keeps playing while you build a team or change settings. Close the player with its X; starting the game stops the music. The music plays in the launcher, so the game doesn't need to be set up or running.

Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness: pick Colosseum or XD on the Play page, and the launcher sets up and plays that game from your own North American disc (GXXE01). Each game has its own setup folder, disc and memory card, and your Colosseum setup stays as it was. If you saved XD on Colosseum's memory card in an earlier Beta, that save moves to XD's own card by itself, after a backup. XD is early: its renderer, display, controller, frame rate, widescreen, HD text, fast-forward and Skip movies settings apply, and so does Later generations under Gameplay: its Gen 4 battle rules, Pokémon and moves come to XD from your Colosseum disc, each Gen 4 Pokémon looking and sounding like one of XD's own. Colosseum's other extras, such as HD trainer models and language packs, are hidden while XD is chosen.

The Play page shows both games, split by a diagonal line: the game you choose fills most of the window in full colour, and the other waits faded at the side. XD has its own painting, the wrecked S.S. Libra in the desert under the moon. Each side shows that game's title logo, read from your own disc (in HD when the HD textures have it), or its name until you've chosen its disc: large in the middle of the side you chose, above Play, and large in the middle of the other side's strip too; while you set a game up, its logo waits small at the top to leave room for the steps. Click the other side or its logo and the line sweeps across, the logos gliding and growing or shrinking into place with it; on a controller, press X (Square on PlayStation).
Choosing the other game's disc switches the Play page to that game, instead of turning the disc down.
Saves: Pokémon XD saves export to Dolphin as a .gci file and import from one, as Colosseum's do. Choose XD on the Play page, then use Import or Export on the Saves tab.
Discord: Pokémon XD shows on your Discord profile too, with the place you're in, the trainer you're battling and your lead Pokémon, when Discord activity is on under Settings.

Pokémon XD: battle animation speed and Skip battle animations, Quick moves and quick status effects, shiny Shadow Pokémon and Choose starter now work in XD too, from the same settings under Gameplay. In XD a Shadow Pokémon can be shiny, which the original never allows, and a New Game asks whether to begin with Eevee.

Pokémon XD: Generation 4 Pokémon take their models and cries from your Battle Revolution disc in XD too, Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can evolve as in Platinum, and Pokémon packs work in XD. All of it is made from your Colosseum disc, so set that up as well.

Online: Pokémon XD battles online too, with a party from the team builder, which reads its Pokémon from your Colosseum disc. Tick Colosseum and XD players can join when you create a room, and a player of either game can battle you. XD's online battles have Colosseum's turn and battle timers, the Pokémon selection screen with team preview, the trainers' screens before and after a battle, and the sleep and HP clauses. In a room for both games every Pokémon is one both games have the same: the 386 Pokémon of the third generation, no Shadow Pokémon or Shadow moves, and only held items both games have, so the battle goes the same on both screens. The launcher says what a party would have to change before you create or join one, and a Story party's other Pokémon stay home. Rooms for both games don't have Platinum's rules yet, and both players need the same version of the games.

Pokémon XD: the randomizer works in XD too, from the same settings under Gameplay. It can swap your Eevee, the Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon, and the Pokémon traded to you and Mt. Battle's Chikorita, Cyndaquil and Totodile; Lugia, the Shadow Togepi you're given, Poké Spots, Quick Battle and the battle CDs stay as they are. The launcher reads your XD save's seed, and Show spoilers works for an XD run.

Online: your Story party works in Pokémon XD too. Choose XD on the Play page, and the Online page offers the party from your XD save, each Pokémon with its moves, nature, IVs, EVs, held item and nickname; Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.

Game Boy Advance: link your Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed or LeafGreen save to Pokémon XD too, and trade at the Trade Center in a Pokémon Center's basement. Set it up under Settings → Game Boy Advance, on socket 2.

Pokémon XD: the Pokédex and the Jukebox work in XD too, read from your XD disc. The Pokédex shows XD's own models, sprites and cries, and says how XD gives each Pokémon: your Eevee, a trade or Mt. Battle reward, a Shadow Pokémon to snag, a Poké Spot, or an evolution. The Jukebox plays the songs of XD's own sound test, looping as the game does.

Pokémon XD: HD textures work in XD too: every texture on XD's disc, upscaled 4× the way Colosseum's are, from Pokémon, trainers' faces and menus to every town. With HD textures on under Settings → Graphics, XD downloads them the next time you play it: about 3.8 GB, in two parts.
Online: Beta now builds Colosseum and Pokémon XD from the same newest game, so players of either game can join a room for both games.

Battle Revolution assets: the launcher checks the disc file you choose straight away. A file that isn't Pokémon Battle Revolution, such as your Colosseum disc, another Wii game or a ZIP, is turned down with the reason in a banner under Settings → Gameplay and in the Generation 4 prompt, instead of failing minutes into making the assets, and a copy that looks cut short gets a warning. A wrong disc chosen before shows a banner on the Play page too.
game: Frame rate: Pokémon XD's overworld and battles run at 60 fps too, where they used to stay at 30, at the original game's speed. Choose 30 or 60 fps under Frame rate in Settings.

Pokémon XD: press A to skip The Pokémon Company and Genius Sonority logos and the opening movie, as in Colosseum, and in widescreen the two logos fill the screen with their background colour instead of black bars.

Pokémon XD: HD text draws XD's text sharp from the Inter typeface, as it does Colosseum's, where it used to only smooth the original letters. It's on by default; choose Text under Gameplay to change it.
Pokémon XD: fixed your character stuttering while walking or running at 60 fps.
Online: in a room for both games, Colosseum makes every Pokémon by the same list of Pokémon, moves and held items as XD does, so both games battle with the same Pokémon.
Online battles now check the battle itself at every turn, so two games that drift apart end the battle instead of playing on with different HP.
Pokémon XD: fixed battles between two of the game's trainers never ending, such as ZOOK and ARDOS at Gateon Port, where neither ever chose a move.
Pokémon XD: fixed walls and furniture in the HQ lab popping in and the room looking squeezed at the 16:10 screen format.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing as it started on some Linux PCs, with some graphics drivers and overlays.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing in battle while it loaded a Pokémon or a move, such as when a Generation 4 Pokémon used Quick Attack.
Pokémon XD: fixed Pokémon and trainers disappearing in battles with Generation 4 Pokémon, leaving only a shadow or part of a trainer's hair.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game staying on a black screen as it started on Windows.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game freezing on a dimmed screen when you saved in some buildings, such as the house where you get an evolution stone and the diner in Gateon Port.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing when you opened Pokémon Storage at a PC. Generation 4 Pokémon and Pokémon from packs show as the Pokémon they stand in for in the boxes.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing after you had moved between rooms and areas about 64 times in one session, such as when leaving a house in Agate Village.

launcher: Later generations: play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules and add the 107 Generation 4 Pokémon. Turn each on under Settings → Gameplay.
Battle Revolution assets: Generation 4 Pokémon take their looks and cries from your own Battle Revolution disc. Without it, a Colosseum Pokémon stands in for each.
Team builder: give each Pokémon its own moves, held item, ability, nature, EVs and IVs. Bring teams in or out as Pokémon Showdown text. Open it with New party or Edit on the Online tab.
Online formats: Orre Colosseum, Hoenn Stadium and Gen 3 OU rooms, with their clauses and bans. Casual stays as it was, Customise changes any rule, and a room can be a best of 3 or 5.
Online timers: a room can have a turn timer and a battle timer, set when you create it.
Legal Pokémon: format rooms check each Pokémon's moves, held item, EVs and IVs, and say what's wrong. A host can turn the check off under Customise.

Generation 4 online: any room can play by Platinum's rules, and a Generation 4 party battles there with that generation's Pokémon, moves and held items. Choose the rules when you create a room, and Generation 4 at the top of the team builder.
Online battles: both players need this version of the launcher.
Pokémon packs: add Pokémon of your own making, with their own stats, moves, model, sprites and cry. Open the packs folder from the Pokédex, then pick one as a starter or let the randomizer choose it.
Pokédex: models look as they do in the game and blink, every Pokémon has a Shiny look, and Cry plays its cry. It also shows what a Pokémon evolves from.
Randomizer: a run can include Generation 4 Pokémon and the Pokémon of your packs. Tick Gen 4 and Pokémon packs under Randomizer.
Language: play in French, German, Spanish or Italian, or with a fan translation. Choose it under Settings → Gameplay.

Game Boy Advance: link a Generation 3 save to trade Pokémon, register a team and spend Poké Coupons. It works with Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed and LeafGreen saves, chosen under Settings → Game Boy Advance, with no GBA BIOS or Game Pak.
Fast-forward: one press of L + R can keep it on, and it runs from 2× to 8×. Set both under Settings → Gameplay.

HD textures: an updated pack keeps the grain of ground and walls and the soft edges of move effects. It also fixes black lines in floors and dark edges on some textures. About 1.9 GB, it downloads the next time you play with HD textures on.
Windows: the game's program has its own icon. The launcher also says before building when the Setup files folder's path has an &, which the build can't use.
When the game stops itself after an error, the launcher says why.
Fixed the game drawing with OpenGL instead of Vulkan on a Steam Deck and other Linux PCs with a newer Mesa.

changes: Generation 4 battle rules: battles play as in Pokémon Platinum, with moves physical or special by themselves, its damage, abilities, held items such as Life Orb and Choice Scarf, and Generation 4's moves. The move list shows whether a move is physical, special or status.

Generation 4 Pokémon: the game's own Pokémon learn moves and evolve as in Platinum, so Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can become Yanmega, Ambipom and Mamoswine. The Move Deleter at Mt. Battle can also make a Pokémon remember a level-up move.
Choose starters: a New Game asks whether to begin with Espeon and Umbreon. Say No to pick any two Pokémon. Turn the question off under Gameplay in the launcher.
Quick moves: press Z (R1 or RB) in battle to open your moves, then A, B, X or Y to use one. Buttons show as your controller or keyboard has them. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
Quick status effects: a status condition or stat change shows where the move hit, without its own camera shot. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
The PC has 10 boxes instead of 3, room for 300 Pokémon. Backups keep them all, and a save exported for Dolphin takes boxes 1 to 3.
Shiny Pokémon: a Shadow Pokémon that will be shiny once snagged looks shiny in battle, and Espeon and Umbreon can be shiny from a New Game. Both have switches under Gameplay.
Online battles: Battle Mode's screens surround a battle. Both trainers show before it, you pick your Pokémon on the game's own selection screen when the room has team preview, and the results follow.
Online rules: battles can be doubles and play by Battle Mode's clauses. They now have critical hits and Soul Dew's boost, as the original game's link battles do.
Randomizer: a Shadow Pokémon or trainer's Pokémon that held the item for its type now holds the one for its new type.
Fixed a number showing instead of the move's name when a Pokémon forgets a move in battle.
Fixed the gold labels on the save and Continue screens showing red.
Fixed the sandstorm, strong sunlight, the PDA and the name screen not filling widescreen.
Fixed a stretched box around Sweet Scent's and Confusion's ripple in widescreen.
Fixed the PDA's Snag List showing the original game's Shadow Pokémon in a randomized run.
Fixed the arrow keys and WASD picking nothing on the Pokémon selection screen before a battle.
Fixed PlayStation controllers stopping in the game on Windows a few seconds after it started.
Fixed the game crashing on Mac when a Pokémon's Wish came true.
Fixed a dull echo trailing behind move sounds such as Sing and Attract.
Fixed the game crashing at start-up without a reason when it couldn't read its disc file. It now says what's wrong.
Fixed setup failing with Xcode 26 or pandoc installed, or when Vulkan's downloads fail.

launcher: Online battles: open a room or join one on the new Online tab and battle another player, at level 50 or 100 with 3 or 6 Pokémon each. Build named parties of six from your Pokédex, and your game waits in the stadium until someone joins. The room list updates by itself, and Refresh checks right away.

Story party: battle online with the Pokémon you travel with. The Online tab shows the party in your save, set apart at the top, and brings each one along with its moves, nature, stats, ability, held item and nickname, at the room's level. A party of 3 to 5 can take rooms of 3 each, and Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.
The top bar shows how many players are online. It comes from an anonymous check-in you can turn off under Settings → Launcher.

Show on Discord: while you play, your Discord profile shows where you are in Orre with a picture of the place, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, and online battles show your opponent. The Discord app needs to be open. Turn it off under Settings → Launcher.

Pokédex: browse all 386 Pokémon from your own disc, turn their 3D models around, play their motions and see their shiny looks. It also shows how you can get each one, and locks those the game keeps out of reach. Find it in the new Pokédex tab.

Randomizer: start a New Game with different starters, Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon and gifts, chosen by a seed you can share. Limit it to the generations you like, keep Pokémon about as strong as those they replace, or leave legendaries out. Your save keeps its seed, so fights stay the same when you try again. Find it under Gameplay.
Export a save: carry on in Dolphin with a .gci file of your game. Find it in the Saves tab.
Battle animations: a speed slider from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1, with 1.5× as the new default, and a Skip battle animations switch that greys it out. Find them under Gameplay.

Macs with Apple Silicon: the game now builds as a native program and draws with Metal, so it runs faster and Rosetta is no longer needed. Metal is the new default renderer on these Macs; Vulkan and OpenGL are still under Graphics. Intel Macs stay on Vulkan.
Fixed the portable launcher on Windows never finding the game's crash reports, so Settings → Launcher can now copy them for a bug report.
Fixed game updates started from Steam filling the activity log with Steam overlay errors, which could also hide why a build failed.
Fixed a crash report on Linux and the Steam Deck when you closed the game with Stop in Steam.

changes: Online battles: two players' games play one battle, with both choosing their moves at the same time, from the launcher's Online tab. A Story party's Pokémon keep their moves, nature, stats, ability, held item, nickname and Poké Ball, at the battle's level.
Save anywhere: the menu you open with Start has a new SAVE option above EXIT. It saves where you stand, and Continue puts you back on that spot.
Randomizer: a new save can be a randomized run, and the save keeps its seed.
Rui and most trainers now have their detailed models in the field too, with sharper faces and real fingers.
Battle animations can run at any speed from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1.
Macs with Apple Silicon: the game runs natively, and the wipe into a trainer battle plays in full instead of going black.
The game tells the launcher where you are, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, for Show on Discord.
When Vulkan can't start on Linux, the game now tries the desktop's other window system before falling back to OpenGL, and the message says why Vulkan couldn't start.
In widescreen, the menu you open with Start now sits at the right edge of the screen, as it does in 4:3.
Fixed Pokémon getting a different nature and gender than a GameCube would give them at the same moment, which also threw off the random rolls after it, such as trainers' teams and damage.
Fixed the game not opening its window on Linux with newer graphics drivers, and that error calling the game Super Mario Sunshine.
Fixed people and objects disappearing near the sides of the screen in widescreen.
Fixed the arrow for picking a target sitting away from the status panels in widescreen.
Fixed the stripes of Yes/No boxes stopping short, and the Poké Ball in a text box's corner drawing outside the box, in widescreen.
Fixed Pokémon blinking twice as often at 60 fps, which also used up the game's random numbers faster than on a GameCube.

launcher: HD models: Wes uses his detailed model in the field. Turn it off under Graphics.
The game now builds from the port's own copy of the decompilation.

changes: Wes now has his detailed battle model while walking around, with a sharper face and real fingers.
Fixed the Pokémon faces missing from the Battle Now team screen.
Fixed opposing trainers misjudging a side's conditions and level-based moves.
Fixed the second trainer on a side being mistaken for the first.
Fixed Pokémon faces staying in memory after being replaced.
Fixed the Pokédex seen and caught flags on Linux and macOS.
Fixed Poké Ball catch rates on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the blue background on the main menus and save screen stopping short of the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the PC menus leaving black bars at the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the game crashing when entering a new area after playing for a long time.
Fixed Rui getting stuck walking on the spot when you first enter the mayor's house in Phenac City, and people stalling the same way in other cutscenes.

launcher: Battle animations: moves, send-outs and HP bars play at 2× speed by default. Change to normal speed or 4×, or skip them, under Gameplay.
Add to Steam: play from your Steam library, Big Picture or Game Mode, with artwork. Find it on the main screen, on Windows and Linux.
Skip Launcher: Steam can start the game straight away, and --play does the same from any shortcut.
Graphics presets: Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Steam Deck set the picture all at once. Find them under Graphics.
Crash reports: copy the newest report for a bug report, under Launcher. They stay on your computer.

changes: Fixed a box appearing around the white ring in some battle moves. Their ripple effect now works too.
Fixed your partner walking behind you facing the wrong way on Linux and macOS.
Fixed battle timers always showing 0 on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the title menu's selection jumping to the next option instead of sliding on Linux and macOS.
Fixed reflective effects not showing on Linux and macOS, along with the title options' animation and the stick in the P★DA.
Fixed items and Poké Balls saying they were meaningless to use in battle, and the bag jumping to another pocket afterwards.
Fixed shop messages showing the wrong price and item, like nearly 2 billion for one Super Potion. Sales always paid the right amount.
Fixed the game crashing when you pressed Down in the P★DA's Strategy Memo list.
Installing and updating the game downloads less: it no longer fetches two extra repositories to build.
Battle animations can run at 2× or 4× speed or be skipped, with menus at normal speed and text up long enough to read.
Building the game is faster: its code now compiles once instead of twice, on Windows too.
Setting up the game is quicker: the fixes its code needs now come ready-made instead of being worked out on your computer.
Game updates that change only part of the build now reuse more of what was already compiled.
The first game build after this update takes longer, as it starts over with what it keeps between builds.
Fixed new builds on Linux and macOS leaving out small corrections to battle and menu code that only a rebuild picked up.
Fixed the battle move menu showing the first move's PP and type whichever move you highlighted.
The logo movies at startup now fill a widescreen display with their background colour instead of black bars.

launcher: Fixed Windows builds with your own MSYS2, set with the COLO_MSYS2_ROOT environment variable, looking for the game's compiler in a folder that MSYS2 doesn't have.
Fixed a game download stopping at Prepare port source when a newer game commit is chosen under Settings, Manage game, Game source.
Windows builds now use a compiler that also runs on Windows 7, which the previous one could not.
The first game build on Windows after this update takes longer, as it starts over with the new compiler.

changes: Fixed builds reporting success when the game's compiler couldn't run: they now stop and say why.
Fixed a rare build that left out part of the battle menus' code.
Fixed Battle Now's party check overwriting nearby memory, which stopped the game on Arch Linux.
Fixed the game failing as it started when built on Arch Linux and other systems not based on Debian.
Fixed the game not fully unloading map code it had finished with.

launcher: New launcher background: a painted copper engine out in the desert.
Game updates and rebuilds are much faster: the launcher keeps what it compiled and reuses it. Free up space under Settings, Manage game clears it.
Import a Dolphin save: drop your North American .gci save on the Saves tab, or the folder it is in, and carry on from there. Your current saves are backed up first.
Join our Discord server: the Discord button at the top of the launcher opens the invite in your browser.

changes: The first build of the game is faster too.
Fixed the game stopping on macOS when you arrive in Phenac City with HD textures at the highest resolution.

launcher: First release: set up and play the Pokémon Colosseum PC port from your own North American disc on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Three-step setup downloads everything it needs and builds the game on your computer. The disc image never leaves it.
HD textures: all 7,498 of the game's textures upscaled 4×, on by default. Turn them off under Settings, Graphics.
Settings for the screen format, frame rate, picture sharpness, controls, rumble and GameCube controller adapters.
Your saves are backed up before and after you play. Restore one from the Saves tab.

changes: Native PC port with movies, music and sound, HD text, widescreen, 60 fps and Vulkan or OpenGL rendering.
